current_answer: For the September 15–16 FOMC decision, the directly observed Polymarket contract displayed 62% for a 25-basis-point increase and 38% for no change when accessed at 13:40 UTC on September 10. Against the matched 21:10 UTC September 9 snapshot, the named increase row was 7 percentage points higher and the no-change row 8 points lower; the pool did not capture a quote around PPI, so it does not assign the move to the release. BLS reported August final-demand PPI up 0.4% in the month and 5.4% over 12 months. CPI is the next scheduled official price release; a current CME FedWatch percentage was not captured because its live grid remains inside an unreadable iframe.

summary: Polymarket's September contract displayed 62% for a 25 bp increase and 38% for no change when accessed September 10, 2026, 13:40 UTC.
Against the September 9, 21:10 UTC snapshot, the named increase row rose 7 percentage points and the no-change row fell 8 points; no cause is claimed.
BLS reported August final-demand PPI up 0.4% in the month and 5.4% over 12 months.
August CPI is scheduled for September 11 at 08:30 ET, before the September 15–16 FOMC meeting.
CME FedWatch remains separately labelled and unquoted because its live grid did not render in this check.
uncertainty: Polymarket did not display a separate quote timestamp; the 13:40 UTC access time is not a closing quote.
Other listed outcome rows were small and rounded; displayed rows should not be forced into an exact 100% distribution.
CME FedWatch's live outcome grid remained unavailable to the read-only renderer, so no current futures-implied percentage or cross-market spread is reported.
The pool did not capture a Polymarket quote immediately before or after the PPI release, so the observed sequence is not evidence that PPI caused it.
PPI is one official release; CPI and the Committee's decision remain ahead.
freshness_note: Direct prediction-market snapshot accessed September 10, 2026, 13:40 UTC, after the official PPI release. The contract price can change continuously; recheck after CPI or material Fed communication.
